newsitem.title: UK: UK Referendum Party targets pro-Europe politicians.
newsitem.headline: UK Referendum Party targets pro-Europe politicians.

text.p: Britain's small anti-Europe Referendum Party on Wednesday launched an advertising campaign to expose the views of leading politicians on the divisive issue of European Union (EU).
The party, formed last year by billioniare businessman Sir James Goldsmith, wants a referendum on whether Britain should remain a member of the EU.
Political analysts say it could eat away at support for Prime Minister John Major's ruling Conservative Party ahead of a May 1 general election by capitalising on scepticism over Europe.
Referendum Party chairman Lord Alistair McAlpine told a news conference that many Conservative and opposition Labour Party MPs were deceiving the electorate as to their pro-EU views.
"It is in the public interest that the true views of the candidates on the vital issue of Europe are revealed to their electorate," McAlpine said. "This campaign is in the interest of truth."
The full-page adverts say that a vote for certain MPs, such as Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine, is "a vote for Brussels" and a betrayal of British independence.

The adverts target about 100 candidates who are on record as voting against a plebiscite on the Maastricht Treaty, for an increase in Britain's contribution to the EU budget, in favour of a single European currency and those who wanted an increase in Spanish and Dutch fishing rights in British waters.
McAlpine admitted that the adverts may actually increase support for some candidates once their stated view on the European Union was publicised.

Britain's role in the EU has been a sensitive issue for both Conservatives and Labour. Both parties officially support a "wait and see" policy on joining a single European currency but the Conservatives have been torn apart by internal wrangling on the issue.
The adverts will appear in local papers across Britain at a cost of about 100,000 pounds ($160,300) following "very serious legal advice".
